https://www.geosuper.tv/latest/58174-fur.text: Boxing Fury beat Wach ahead of Joshua showdown Fury vs Wach fight in Thailand was not televised By Web Desk July 25, 2026 Tyson Fury in action with Mariusz Wach at Max Muay Thai Stadium in Pattaya on July 24, 2026. — Reuters Former world heavyweight champion Tyson Fury forced Polish boxer Mariusz Wach to retire in a tune-up fight on Friday for his blockbuster showdown against Briton Anthony Joshua later in 2026. The bout in Thailand was not televised, but will feature in the Netflix reality show "At Home with The Furys". About 1,500 fans were there at the event at the Max Muay Thai Stadium in Pattaya. Wach had lost seven of his last 10 fights, and the 46-year-old was unable to continue at the start of the eighth round. "I went through my test tonight. Let's see if he can get through his," Fury said. Fury, who turns 38 in August, has a professional record of 36-2, suffering his only losses in two fights with Ukraine's Oleksandr Usyk in 2024. Joshua, also a former world heavyweight champion, is set to face Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia today. Many expected the Gypsy King to fly straight to Jeddah for the AJ fight after Joshua invited him to a face-off. Instead, Fury said he was going home. "I've got to face off with my wife. I've got to iron when I get home. I've been away for six out of the last seven months", he said. "I'm not going to Jeddah, I'm going home to my wife and kids. I'm going to regroup and hopefully we'll have a big fight signed next week." Questions still linger over where the all-British fight would be materialised, with promoter Eddie Hearn saying Joshua's contract stipulates the UK, but industry whispers suggest a venue in America. "We'll head wherever we're going to head," Fury said. "Who knows? It could be in Vegas, New York, Ireland, London. Who knows where the fight's going to be?" Photograph: Mohamed Siali/EPA View image in fullscreen Moroccan police were seen monitoring dozens of migrants on the outskirts of the border town of Fnideq on Saturday. Photograph: Mohamed Siali/EPA Morocco Moroccan police arrest more than 100 people as they attempt to enter Ceuta Border security tightened after social media posts call for another mass crossing into Spain’s north African territory Reuters Sat 15 Aug 2026 14.08 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Moroccan police have arrested 111 people as they tried to enter Spain’s north African territory of Ceuta, amid ⁠tightened security on both sides after social media posts ​called for another mass crossing. The attempted crossing on Saturday came two weeks after more than 72,000 migrants surged into Ceuta , causing tensions within the EU and prompting anti-immigration rhetoric among far-right parties worldwide. At least 96 people died trying to ⁠reach European soil. A source in Morocco’s interior ministry told news agency Reuters that those detained included 109 migrants from sub-Saharan Africa and two Moroccan citizens arrested in or around Fnideq, the Moroccan city near Ceuta. Moroccan police used teargas to disperse groups of migrants ⁠gathered on hills about 1.9 miles (3km) from the border, according to Spanish news agency EFE. Reuters later saw hundreds of police officers, some in riot gear and others in plainclothes, returning from the hills outside ​Fnideq. EFE and Spanish state broadcaster TVE said Morocco’s interior ministry ordered their journalists ‌to leave Fnideq immediately, without providing an explanation. View image in fullscreen Witnesses said they saw teargas being fired at migrants on hills near the border. Photograph: Jalal Morchidi/EPA In Ceuta, ‌Spanish soldiers guarded supermarkets while police patrolled the main streets. The city was calmer than in the days after the deadly crossing attempt on 30 July. Madrid has ‌since installed a maritime barrier and deployed more than 500 additional police officers from mainland Spain , raising the total in Ceuta to more than 1,600. The interior ministry said the reinforcements would remain for as long as needed. “We’ll continue to deploy whatever personnel are necessary to restore normality as soon as possible and prevent events like those of 30 July from happening again,” Spain’s interior minister, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, said on Thursday. About 5,000 migrants remained in Ceuta , the minister added. Reuters saw hundreds sheltering from scorching heat under makeshift bamboo shelters on the urban beach of El Trampolin. View image in fullscreen Migrants seen sheltering from the sun on El Trampolin beach in Ceuta. Photograph: Jorge Guerrero/AFP/Getty Images Grande-Marlaska said migrants who entered irregularly would not be allowed to stay in the territory, travel to mainland Spain or ‌obtain legal status, except in rare cases involving extreme vulnerability. Those without a right to remain would be returned to Morocco, he added. Earlier this week, Rabat said it was monitoring “the circulation of social media posts and messages of unknown origin” calling for a mass crossing ​on 15 August, warning it would prosecute organisers and participants. A Reuters witness saw reinforced security near the border, including police vans with wire shields and road checkpoints. Local media reported similar measures near Melilla, another Spanish territory in north Africa. Authorities prevented several groups from boarding trains and buses to northern Morocco in cities such as Casablanca, Fez and Kenitra. However, witnesses told Reuters that some migrants from sub-Saharan Africa were bypassing security checkpoints by taking mountain routes towards Fnideq. One witness said the schools in Fnideq had been turned into accommodation for security forces deployed near the ⁠border. BlaÅ¾ys / LRT A Lithuanian priest whose criminal case has been referred to court is accused of committing sexual offenses against minors over a 23-year period, with 11 people recognised as victims, prosecutors said Tuesday. The Vilnius Regional Prosecutorâs Office said the priest faces charges related to 34 intentional offenses, including crimes against sexual self-determination and integrity, offenses against children and crimes against public morality. âThe data in the case indicate that these crimes were committed, as stated in the indictment, from 2002 until 2025 â 23 years,â said Justas Laucius, chief prosecutor of the Vilnius Regional Prosecutorâs Office. According to prosecutors, the priest is accused of 13 incidents involving providing alcohol to a child or children, nine incidents involving the exploitation of children for pornography, four cases of sexually abusing people under 16, and three cases of satisfying sexual desires for payment while violating a minorâs sexual freedom. He is also accused of two incidents of raping a minor and one incident involving the rape of a young child. âEleven people have been recognized as victims in this case. At the time of the alleged offenses, they were between 12 and 18 years old,â Laucius told reporters. The case has been referred to the Vilnius Regional Court. Prosecutors said most of the alleged offenses occurred in residences belonging to the Roman Catholic Church where the priest lived at the time. âNot all of the crimes were committed within the territory of the Archdiocese of Vilnius, but most of them were,â Laucius said. âWe are talking about six separate locations in Lithuania.â Lithuaniaâs Criminal Code provides for a prison sentence of up to 15 years for the most serious sexual offense alleged in the case, prosecutors said. The priest has been ordered not to leave Lithuania and has surrendered his passport. His rights to dispose of real estate have also been restricted to secure potential civil claims by the alleged victims. Second priest faces pornography charge Prosecutors also said another criminal case involving a Catholic priest was referred to the Vilnius City District Court in June. The priest is accused of possessing child pornography. He has also been ordered not to leave Lithuania. Prosecutors said there are no victims in that case. âThe case concerns pornographic material depicting a child or a person presented as a child,â Laucius said, describing the evidence as visual material. Laucius said prosecutors had cooperated constructively with the Archdiocese of Vilnius in both cases. Both priests have been removed from their duties and are no longer engaged in public pastoral work, he said. The Lithuanian Bishopsâ Conference said in July that five canonical investigations into possible sexual abuse cases were underway in the countryâs dioceses at the end of 2025. Two had been launched in 2025 and three in earlier years. Laucius said alleged crimes of this nature can take decades to come to light because victims often do not report them. âThere is a high level of latency â nobody complained,â he said, adding that criminological factors may also play a role. âIn my opinion, that is one of the main reasons.â Archdiocese in cooperation with law enforcement The Archdiocese of Vilnius said Tuesday it was cooperating with law enforcement and conducting canonical investigations. âThe Archdiocese of Vilnius has cooperated responsibly with law enforcement agencies and, out of respect for the judicial process, taking into account the sensitive situation of the victims and seeking to protect their privacy, will continue this cooperation,â it said in a statement. It also said it had initiated canonical investigations and notified the Holy See about the suspected crimes. âWe have no doubt that the court and the canonical process will answer all questions, and those who have committed crimes will be punished accordingly,â the archdiocese stated. The priests against whom charges have been brought have been and remain suspended from their duties, it assured. âEvery report of possible inappropriate behaviour toward a child or a vulnerable person is shocking and painful. Behind every such report is, first and foremost, a person â their experiences and pain, and sometimes years of suffering and trauma. It affects not only the victim and their loved ones, but also wounds the entire community,â Archbishop Gintaras GruÅ¡as of Vilnius is quoted in the statement.
